sentences.sentence: Art is work made with form and intent so it can be seen, heard, or used as more than a tool.
Religion is a shared set of beliefs and practices about what a community treats as sacred.
Philosophy is reasoned inquiry into knowledge, value, mind, and what exists.
Science is a method of building and testing models of the world against observation.
Mathematics is the study of number, structure, and proof, independent of any one physical example.

Africa is the second-largest continent, crossed by the equator and home to the Sahara and the Nile.
Antarctica is the southern polar continent, covered by ice and holding most of Earth's fresh water as ice.
Asia is the largest continent, stretching from the Mediterranean to the Pacific.
Europe is the western peninsula of Eurasia, bounded by the Atlantic, Arctic, and Mediterranean.
North America is the northern continent of the Western Hemisphere, from the Arctic to the Isthmus of Panama.
South America is the southern continent of the Western Hemisphere, dominated by the Andes and the Amazon basin.
Australia is both a continent and a country, the largest landmass of Oceania.
The Pacific is the largest ocean, lying between Asia and the Americas.
The Atlantic is the ocean between the Americas and Europe-Africa.
The Indian Ocean lies between Africa, Asia, and Australia.
The Arctic Ocean is the smallest ocean, centered on the North Pole and often covered by sea ice.
The Nile is a long African river that flows north to the Mediterranean.
The Amazon is the great South American river whose basin holds the largest tropical rainforest.
The Mississippi is the chief river of the central United States, flowing south to the Gulf of Mexico.
The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia, flowing east across China to the East China Sea.
The Sahara is the large hot desert of North Africa.
The Himalaya is the high mountain system of South Asia, raised by the collision of India with Eurasia.
The Andes is the long mountain chain along the west of South America.
The Alps is the high mountain system of south-central Europe.
The Rocky Mountains is the major north-south range of western North America.
The equator is the great circle of zero latitude, midway between the poles.
Latitude is angular distance north or south of the equator.
Longitude is angular distance east or west of a prime meridian.
The prime meridian in common use runs through Greenwich and defines zero longitude.
The tropics are the belt between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
A geographic pole is where Earth's axis meets the surface.
A volcano is a vent where magma and gas reach the surface.
An earthquake is a sudden slip of rock along a fault that radiates seismic waves.
Plate tectonics is the motion of rigid lithospheric plates over the mantle.
A fossil is a preserved remain or trace of an organism from a past geologic age.
Dinosaurs were a diverse group of Mesozoic reptiles; birds are their living descendants.
A mammal is a vertebrate that feeds young with milk and usually has hair.
A bird is a feathered, egg-laying vertebrate, most of which fly.
A fish is an aquatic vertebrate that typically breathes with gills and has fins.
An insect is a six-legged arthropod with a body in three parts.
Bacteria are prokaryotic microorganisms without a nucleus.
A virus is a genetic package that replicates only inside a host cell.
The brain is the central organ of the nervous system in vertebrates.
The heart is the muscular pump that moves blood through the body.
Blood is the circulating fluid that carries oxygen, nutrients, and waste in animals.
